title: SURE Acceptance Report
description: The release contract in evaluation/acceptance-manifest.json, with the outcome actually observed for every case. Produced by sure_core::acceptance_report and driven over the corpus by crates/sure-core/tests/acceptance_report_runner.rs. A row's `observed` is what the machinery that grades that case produced when it was run; it is never a copy of the manifest's own requirement.

schema_version.description: Version of this report's shape. Bumped when the shape changes in a way an older reader would get wrong.

corpus.description: Which contract, and which corpus, this report is against.

manifest_digest.description: The digest that ties a report to the exact contract it was produced against: `sure_core::fingerprint::digest` under the domain `sure.acceptance-corpus.v1`, with the manifest file's bytes as its single length-prefixed field. An edited contract changes this value, so a report cannot silently remain green against a contract it was not produced from.

cases.description: One row per manifest case, sorted by id. Every case exactly once: a case with no row, or two, is a failure of this report and not a warning.

required.description: What the manifest asks for. Read from the manifest and labelled as the requirement, never as an outcome.

observed.description: What was measured, or why nothing callable could measure it. `status` is the discriminator: `observed` carries severity and statements, `cannot_confirm` carries what is missing and what would have to change.

axis.description: Which rule the case is graded on. `severity`: the manifest states a required severity and the case is met when the grading machinery reaches that level or a heavier one. `outcome`: the manifest names an outcome and the case is met when the machinery produces it.

severity.description: The severity the grading machinery reached, in the manifest's own vocabulary. `null` on an observed severity-axis row means nothing fired at all, which is a measurement and cannot meet a requirement.

statements.description: The measured facts the row rests on. Every value in one was produced by the surface named in `surfaces`, or read out of the fixture file named in an anchor.

surfaces.description: The functions and modules that observed this case. Empty only where the case could not be observed, and then `statements` says what was read instead.

anchors.description: Where a reader who disagrees can go and look.

comparison.description: The requirement and the observation side by side, with the measured value in it.

fixtures_without_a_case.description: Directories in the corpus that correspond to no manifest case, named rather than skipped into invisibility, with the reason each one does not have to.

limitations.description: What this report does not know, said in the report rather than only in a commit message.
